hero.title: Horsemen *insuring horsemen*
hero.lede: We’re riders, owners, officials and event organizers who insure horses, farms and horse businesses, and we explain it in plain English. We work with highly rated carriers to fit coverage to how you ride, board, teach or compete.

facts.label: Medical or surgical, per horse per term

sections.title: Coverage *for every kind of horse life*

items.title: Mortality & theft
items.text: Reimburses you if a covered horse dies or is stolen, for horses from 24 hours to 20 years old. Installment plans available.

items.title: Medical & surgical
items.text: Add major medical or surgical coverage to a mortality policy: up to $15,000 per horse per policy term.

items.title: Loss of use & more
items.text: Permanent disability (loss of use), worldwide coverage, prospective foal, stallion infertility, and tack and equipment.

items.title: Horse owner liability
items.text: Up to $1,000,000 per occurrence, with legal defense outside the limits, on or off your property across the U.S. and Canada.

items.title: Commercial equine liability
items.text: For training, showing, teaching, boarding or leasing: $300,000 to $1,000,000 per occurrence, with no liability deductible.

items.title: Care, custody or control
items.text: Covers other people’s horses in your care, which most liability policies leave out.

items.title: Farm & ranch property
items.text: Barns, fencing, equipment and the farm exposures a homeowner’s policy may not cover.

items.title: Shows, clubs & associations
items.text: Packages for riding clubs, associations, and horse shows and events.

items.title: Workers’ comp & umbrella
items.text: Workers’ compensation, commercial vehicles and trailers, and excess limits up to $5,000,000.

items.title: Care for your horse first
items.text: See to your horse’s immediate needs, which often means calling your veterinarian.

items.title: Call us or your carrier right away
items.text: Your policy requires prompt notice of any injury or illness. Call (866) 780-3713; after hours, choose the emergency option.

items.title: Have the details ready
items.text: Policy number, the horse’s name, what happened and when, your vet’s name and number, and how to reach you.

items.title: If your horse dies
items.text: A necropsy (an autopsy) must be done to find the cause of death. Ask us how to arrange it.

sections.title: Insurance people *who ride*

image.alt: The LEGIS team standing together in a green pasture with a horse

body: Our team represents different breeds and disciplines, from the hunter/jumper ring and eventing to reining and ranch riding, and we bring that horse sense to insurance. We know horses aren’t one-size-fits-all, and neither are the people who own them.
We work with a range of highly rated carriers, and we stay with you from your very first policy through every change in horse ownership or business. We’re a phone call or an email away.

items.q: Doesn’t my homeowner’s policy cover my horse?
items.a: Often not. If your horse gets loose, runs onto a road and causes an accident, or kicks someone, you could be liable for damages a homeowner’s policy won’t pay. Horse owner liability is written for exactly that.

items.q: I only teach a few lessons a month. Do I need commercial coverage?
items.a: Yes. Teaching, training, showing or boarding horses for others, or leasing your horse, counts as commercial, whether it’s a few lessons a month or a large show barn.

items.q: How do I insure a horse?
items.a: Call or email us. In most cases a mortality application and a statement of condition are all it takes; with prior medical history we may need a few more documents, and we’ll guide you.

items.q: Which carriers do you work with?
items.a: Highly rated carriers that specialize in the horse industry, including Great American, Berkley Equine, American Equine Insurance Group and The Hartford.
